Layouts scored and tuned by search

Every base below is produced by simulated annealing over legal placements, scored against measurable properties of the arrangement. Counts, footprints, ranges and levels all come from the shipped game data at 18.400.11. Drag to pan, pinch or scroll to zoom, and flip between the seeded base and the tuned one to see what the search changed.

▲
SCORED ON GEOMETRY, NOT BATTLES
The optimizer maximises coverage, town hall depth, enclosure and balance — not simulated destruction. A base scoring 0.53 is demonstrably better arranged than one scoring 0.14 by this ruler; how it survives a real attack needs the simulator, which is not built yet.

What the search changed

MeasureSeed TunedΔWhat it means

Balance is where nearly all the gain comes from. The seeded bases were lopsided — strong on one side, thin on another — and a base that only holds from one direction is exactly the failure a naive score would happily produce. It is measured as the weakest quadrant's defence density over the strongest.

How the search works

  • Simulated annealing over three mutations: translate a structure, swap two of equal footprint, nudge a wall segment.
  • Every candidate is checked for legality before it is scored — bounds, overlap, per-town-hall counts, walls never on structures. The search cannot emit an illegal base however it mutates; that is asserted, not filtered.
  • Seeded RNG, so a town hall and profile always produce the same base. 12,000 iterations each; all 18 town halls tune in about 3.5 seconds.
  • Profile-weighted. War leans on town hall depth; farming leans on protecting storages. Switch above and the search target changes.

When the simulator is calibrated, battle-based fitness replaces the geometric objective without touching the search — that is what the Objective trait is for.

About the art

Sprites are real, decoded from the game's ASTC atlases. They are assigned by footprint, not identity — mapping a specific building to its own sprite needs the .sc record stream, where name → id is solved but id → texture rectangle is not. So the art is genuine and the sizes are right; a given tower is not necessarily showing its own portrait. Turn Game art off for the plain footprint view.

Export

A base link decodes to 24 bytes — an identifier for a layout already on Supercell's servers, not the layout itself. Offline designs cannot be minted into working links.
